<description>
Closes all holes introduced in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36437 , then adds one more recently developed that involves 2+ honest CPFPs

This will stay in draft, with the plan off peeling off fixes for follow-ups to #36437 until no holes remain, or we decide the holes are not worth filling.

replaces #36369

List of known vectors: https://gist.github.com/instagibbs/880a76535fd802fced9f9a5253cdbb40
</description>

<commits>
47776a909e fuzz: add end-to-end liveness target for parent and child relay

Check that if an honest peer announces the child of an acceptable
parent and child, the child ends up in the mempool within a bounded
time, whatever other peers do. The target drives a real PeerManager
with real messages and validation, which the existing targets cannot,
as they model validation results.

After an adversarial prefix the honest peer only answers requests. With
an outbound honest peer the adversaries keep acting; with an inbound
one they go quiet. Adversary connections are limited, and adversaries
do not refill outbound slots.

Known liveness holes are marked in the target and turn the check off
once opened, including the lost orphan reconsideration fixed in the
next commit.

65b48ba1f1 txorphanage: hand reconsideration over when its announcement is erased

A child that arrives before its parent is kept as an orphan. Once the
parent is accepted on its own, the orphan is put in one randomly chosen
announcer's work set to be retried. If that announcer disconnects or is
evicted first, the orphan is never retried, and re-announcements by the
other announcers don't fetch it again since it is already held. This
keeps e.g. a CPFP child of a parent that pays for itself out of the
mempool until the orphan is evicted, and an announcer can cause it on
purpose.

Hand reconsideration over to the remaining announcer with the lowest
NodeId instead.

Remove its hole from the liveness target.

9ec51af928 p2p: don't add already-known transactions to the reject filter

TX_CONFLICT means the transaction is already known, in the mempool or
confirmed, not that it is invalid. Its wtxid still went into the reject
filter. For a witnessless copy that is also the txid, so if the known
parent then left the mempool before the next block, a child arriving
afterwards was dropped as having a rejected parent. For the honest
version of a parent whose other-witness version is in the mempool, the
honest parent itself was ignored once that version left.

Don't add TX_CONFLICT results to the reject filter. The entry only saved
re-downloading and re-checking a transaction we already have.

Update the rejection-type table for TX_CONFLICT, and remove the hole
from the liveness target.

cf197bf63b p2p: keep orphan after a package feerate failure

When a 1p1c package fails the package feerate check, the child gets a
TX_RECONSIDERABLE result, and ProcessPackageResult passed it to
ProcessInvalidTx, which erased the child from the orphanage for all of
its announcers.

The failure is a property of that pair of wtxids, which
MempoolRejectedPackage already caches, not of the child. The child can
still succeed with another version of the parent, such as the one an
honest announcer holds, so it should stay available.

Skip ProcessInvalidTx for package members with a TX_RECONSIDERABLE
result. A child that is too low feerate on its own is still rejected
when its parent's work set is processed. Remove the hole from the
liveness target.

44009dccf5 txrequest: forget announcements by type, keep orphan parent requests

A reconsiderable rejection of a witnessless copy of a transaction forgot its
wtxid in TxRequestTracker regardless of announcement type, and since that
wtxid equals the txid, it also cancelled every peer's txid-typed request for
the transaction, including orphan resolution requests for a missing parent.
Now only wtxid-typed announcements of that hash are forgotten, so witnessless
parents are treated like witnessed ones, which were never affected since
their wtxid differs from the txid.

ae9cfeb03f p2p: request an orphan's parents again when its retry still misses them

When an orphan's parent is accepted, every request for it is forgotten
and the orphan is queued for a retry. If the parent leaves the mempool
before the retry, the retry fails for missing inputs and nothing
requests the parent again, so the orphan waits until it expires.
Register the orphan's announcers again as candidates for its missing
parents when a retry still misses inputs, and remove the hole from the
liveness target.

73ce30f555 p2p: never check rejections by txid

Orphan handling and txid lookups read the recent rejects filter by txid,
but the filter is keyed by wtxid and a witnessless transaction's wtxid is
its txid, so a rejected witness-stripped copy of any confirmed or mempool
transaction made every orphan spending it be dropped. Never read the
reject filters by txid, and no longer write txids to them: the entry for
TX_INPUTS_NOT_STANDARD has no reader left, and the limit of one
low-feerate parent per orphan, which only ever matched witnessless
parents, goes with the read. This is the change of #33066.

The cost, raised by ajtowns there, is bandwidth for a node whose policy
is stricter than its peers': a parent rejected for a reason that depends
on the txid alone, such as a nonstandard input type, is downloaded again
once per announcer of each of its children until the next block. Each
copy is dropped by wtxid before validation.

This closes the last known hole in the liveness target, so the list of
holes and the switch they turned off are removed from it.

Co-authored-by: glozow <gloriajzhao@gmail.com>

dfa56ba86f p2p: remember nonstandard-input rejections by txid

The previous commit stopped reading rejections by txid, the right
default: a wtxid entry says nothing about other witnesses. One verdict
is a function of the txid alone and is only reached once the inputs
were found, so no copy of a known transaction can produce it:
TX_INPUTS_NOT_STANDARD. Without a txid record of it, a node whose
policy is stricter than its peers' (an unupgraded node after a soft
fork) fetches such a parent once per announcer of each of its children,
holds every descendant in the orphanage until it expires, and repeats
this at every level of a chain, since a held segwit orphan is not
recognised by txid either. Children of a remembered txid are dropped
and remembered too, so a whole subtree costs one download per member.

Keep these txids in a small exact set, cleared on each tip change,
rather than in the bloom filter: a false positive here would drop an
honest child by txid along with its descendants. The set is capped at
10,000 entries; once full, further rejections are not remembered until
the next block, which costs bandwidth and nothing else. This is the
case ajtowns raised on #33066.

077fd92074 fuzz: let the liveness target's honest peer bump its child

The honest peer may now announce child versions that do not pay for the
pair before the one that does, each replacing the previous one as a
wallet bumping the fee would, and answers requests for replaced versions
with notfound. Adversaries can use every version.

This reaches two holes that need a second child from the same honest
peer. They are flagged, and the property is not checked when one opens:

- A completed request for the parent by txid to the honest peer is kept
  while another peer's announcement of the txid is open, and makes the
  honest peer's registration for the bumped child's parent a no-op.
- An older version held for the honest peer after the bumped one is its
  newest orphan, and only the package with it is tried.
